queries.hook: I can't focus, my mind is restless. Inside, my mind won't settle, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.
queries.steady: The mind can be trained slowly, by practice and letting go; each time it wanders, it can be gently brought back.
queries.act: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.

hook.speaker: Arjuna
hook.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
hook.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
hook.line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
hook.translation: Arjuna said: One who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind falls away from yoga before reaching perfection, what end does he come to, Krishna?
hook.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

prasang.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

hook.for_you: Your mind won't settle while you are studying, and a verse was chosen with that weight in mind.

alternates.speaker: Tulsidas
alternates.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram, slowed by shame, quickened by love.
alternates.sanskrit: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
alternates.line: Shame slowed him. But whenever he remembered Ram's nature, his feet moved faster.
alternates.translation: It was as if his mother's wrong held him back, while the strength of devotion drove him on like a patient ox. Whenever he remembered Raghunath's nature, his feet moved faster on the path.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
alternates.sanskrit: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥
alternates.line: Fallen from both sides, does he scatter like a torn cloud, with nowhere to stand?
alternates.translation: Fallen from both, does he not perish like a broken cloud, without support, mighty-armed one, bewildered on the path to Brahman?
alternates.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: After the story of two grieving brothers, Vasishtha tells Rama how worry feeds itself.
verse.sanskrit: चिन्तनेनैधते चिन्ता त्विन्धनेनेव पावकः । नश्यत्यचिन्ततेनैव विनेन्धनमिवानलः ॥
verse.line: Worry grows when you feed it thought, like fire with fuel. Starve it, and it dies down.
verse.translation: Worry grows by thinking, as fire grows with fuel; and it dies by not being thought, as fire dies without fuel.
verse.why: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

prasang.title: Punya consoles his younger brother Pavana after their parents die
prasang.summary: Two brothers live with their parents by the Ganga. When their father and mother die, the elder, Punya, performs the rites calmly while the younger, Pavana, wanders the forest weeping. Punya gently helps him see that the bonds of 'mine' and 'not mine' are made in the mind. Vasishtha draws the lesson: worry grows when fed, and a full mind finds the world full.
prasang.story_hook: When their parents died, one brother quietly lit the funeral fires and the other ran weeping into the forest.
prasang.lesson: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

why: Worry grows when you feed it (Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6)
worry is shown to live on the attention it is fed

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.

words.en: here no stepping back, no destruction

verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: On this path, no beginning is lost and no harm results. Even a small amount of this practice protects from great fear. The tradition reads this as a path of action where every step forward counts, and even a little effort shields one from the fear of birth and death.

why: Even a little of this path protects from great fear.
a small sincere effort already protects

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha describes King Janaka after his awakening, still ruling his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: भविष्यं नानुसंधत्ते नातीतं चिन्तयत्यसौ । वर्तमाननिमेषं तु हसन्नेवानुवर्तते ॥
verse.line: Don't chase the future or brood on the past. Meet this moment with a smile.
verse.translation: He does not chase the future or brood on the past; he simply goes along with the present moment, smiling.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

why: Do not chase the future or brood on the past.
a picture of a mind not living ahead or behind

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: King Ram calls the whole city together and tells them how to treat what he says.
verse.sanskrit: सोइ सेवक प्रियतम मम सोई। मम अनुसासन मानै जोई॥ जौं अनीति कछु भाषौं भाई। तौ मोहि बरजहु भय बिसराई ॥
verse.line: If I say anything wrong, stop me. Don't be afraid.
verse.translation: "The one who follows my teaching is truly my dear servant. But if I say anything unjust, brothers, put aside your fear and stop me."
verse.why: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.

prasang.title: Ram's address to the citizens
prasang.summary: Ram calls his people together and says he speaks without pride of rank: if he says anything wrong, stop him without fear. The way he recommends needs no grand effort, only a simple nature, an honest mind, contentment, and no grudges, no quarrels, no craving and no fear.
prasang.lesson: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.

story.title: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
story.story_hook: High on a mountain lived a crow who had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall.
story.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow arrogant from knowing, and shares in others' joys and sorrows.
story.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.
story.hook_title: An old crow had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall, untroubled
story.teaser: An old crow had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall, untroubled
